title: Admin workspace and permissions
summary: Handle projects and manage the platform according to role.
steps: Use the Admin center entry in the customer portal. Menus follow permissions; a missing entry is not necessarily a fault.

The owner handles privileged configuration; administrators manage business and accounts. Operators handle assigned projects and can also manage announcements and scheduled publication. Backup scheduling and runtime administration require owner permissions.
Administrators can switch between customer and administration documentation here. Reading a guide does not grant the permissions it describes.

faq.question: Why can a colleague see a menu I cannot?
faq.answer: Ask the platform owner to check your role and permissions. Do not bypass restrictions with a shared account.

title: Assignment, progress and requested changes
summary: Work on submitted briefs and distinguish internal notes from customer replies.
steps: Find and open the request under Projects and inspect submitted material. Administrators assign owners; operators work on assigned projects.
Update progress, priority and internal follow-up dates to reflect reality. For customer changes, provide a reason and specify editable sections.
Use project replies for customer-facing communication and internal notes for team follow-up. Verify saved content; read back the result before retrying an uncertain write.

faq.question: Can the previous operator continue after reassignment?
faq.answer: Subsequent requests check the current assignee. The previous operator loses access to process that project; open pages must refresh their state.

title: Publishing and withdrawing deliverables
steps: Open an authorized project and select a deliverable in its delivery section. MP4 and MOV are supported; check the displayed size limit.
Add the relevant note, wait for upload and processing, and verify the published list. Customers download from project details.
Use withdrawal for an incorrect file and verify the outcome. Withdrawal cannot remove copies already downloaded by customers.

faq.question: Should I upload again if the result is uncertain?
faq.answer: Use recovery or refresh to check whether it was saved first. Retrying the same attempt reuses its upload identifier to avoid duplicates.

title: Overview and efficiency definitions
summary: Interpret completion time, sample size and trends.
steps: Select a date range in Overview to inspect submissions, completions and open-request aging.
Average completion time measures total elapsed time from first submission to completion, including customer revisions and waiting. Read it together with the median and valid sample count.
An absent value is not zero. Incomplete history and unknown timestamps must be treated separately rather than used to judge team efficiency.

faq.question: Is this production labor time?
faq.answer: No. It is end-to-end elapsed time, not labor hours or a delivery SLA commitment.

title: Creating accounts and managing organizations
summary: Inspect membership and create users with the organization preselected.
steps: Find an organization and expand its members to inspect names, avatars and roles.
Use Add member or Create member to preselect that organization. Verify the account, role and organization before saving.
Check the impact before disabling or moving an account. Project sharing follows the creator’s current organization, so membership changes can alter shared access.

faq.question: Can customers manage membership?
faq.answer: The customer organization page is read-only. Membership is maintained by authorized administrators.

title: Configuring email and sending a test
summary: Configure SMTP as owner and verify actual receipt.
steps: As platform owner, open Email service under the Messaging settings group, then Configure email.
Enter the SMTP host, STARTTLS port, sender, username, app credential and customer portal domain. Implicit TLS on port 465 is not supported; production domains should use HTTPS.
Save and enable the service, then choose Send test email and confirm the recipient. The test targets the configured sender itself; inspect inbox and spam folders afterwards.
A blank credential normally keeps the existing value. When changing host, port or username, follow the prompt to replace or clear credentials. Never include them in feedback, screenshots or chat.

Configure rolling minute and 24-hour limits (defaults 10/200). Tests and failed attempts also count; restarts or sender changes do not reset usage. Limited messages stay queued and the page refreshes every 15 seconds while showing estimated resumption. Expired links are not replayed. The audit log shows quota values before and after changes.

faq.question: Does Ready mean email was received?
faq.answer: No. Ready means configuration is complete; a successful test means SMTP acceptance. Actual delivery must be confirmed in the inbox.

faq.question: Can a local portal domain be used in production?
faq.answer: It cannot provide publicly accessible customer links. Configure the real public HTTPS domain and test verification and recovery links at deployment.

faq.question: Why can sending fail below the quota?
faq.answer: Platform quotas are local limits, not provider allowances. Inspect failure categories, credentials, connectivity and provider restrictions. Avoid repeated test sends.

title: Missing email and queue troubleshooting
summary: Distinguish pending, retrying and SMTP-accepted messages.
steps: Open Email service and filter by state and message type. First confirm the service is enabled and ready.
Waiting to retry means another attempt is pending. Exhausted retries require configuration and error-category checks. Handed to mail server means SMTP acceptance only.
For authentication errors, check username and app credentials. For connection or TLS errors, check host, STARTTLS port and server network. For recipient rejection, verify the address.

If a notification was not queued, check verified email, subscription switch, categories, unread status and project access. Notification preferences do not control verification or password-security messages.

faq.question: Will the global proxy fix SMTP connectivity?
faq.answer: SMTP currently connects directly and does not use the HTTP outbound proxy. Check connectivity from the server process to the mail host.

title: Configuring multiple OIDC providers
summary: Register callbacks, check metadata and test real sign-in.
steps: As owner, open Settings → Sign-in and integrations → Sign-in methods. Add a provider with bilingual names, issuer, client ID, secret and portal domains.
After the first save, register the exact generated callback URL with the identity provider. Use the authorization-code flow with PKCE S256 support.
Check and enable the provider. Multiple providers can be enabled. A metadata check does not validate secrets or access policies; test linking and sign-in with a test account.
Users first sign in with their platform password and link an external identity. Matching email addresses do not automatically link, register or synchronize roles.

faq.question: Are intranet-only providers supported?
faq.answer: OIDC backend endpoints currently require public HTTPS and reject private-network targets. Intranet-only identity providers are not supported.

faq.question: Is OIDC two-factor authentication?
faq.answer: No. OIDC is an identity protocol; multi-factor requirements depend on the provider’s policy.

title: Form options, characters and voice references
summary: Maintain the choices available in customer forms.
steps: Open the Content settings group and select form options, file categories, character presets or voice references.
Check both Chinese and English labels when editing. Save, then verify the corresponding customer-side choice.
Consider existing projects before disabling or changing choices. Example images and reference voices are not customer deliverables.

faq.question: How should I handle a save conflict?
faq.answer: Read the latest configuration, compare changes and save after deciding what to preserve, rather than overwriting another administrator’s work.

title: Announcements, notifications and feedback
summary: Publish announcements and answer feedback through notifications.
steps: Create and publish notices under Project operations → Announcements. See Creating announcements and choosing placement for audience and dismissal behavior, and Creating and managing scheduled announcements for scheduling.
In Platform feedback, search for the issue, open details and inspect the screenshot, then choose a state and write a reply.
Customers read saved replies in notifications. Changing only the state does not send a reply notification; read back details if saving has an uncertain outcome.

faq.question: Is there a separate feedback chat?
faq.answer: No. Administrator replies are delivered through notifications.

title: Runtime health, storage and outbound proxy
summary: Inspect capacity and configure networking for AI and OIDC.
steps: As owner, open Runtime and network under Operations to inspect health and storage usage details.
Choose direct, system or custom HTTP/HTTPS proxy globally. AI integrations and individual OIDC providers can override that setting.
New requests use saved changes; existing requests are not replayed. A failed proxy does not fall back to direct access, and SMTP and browser traffic are unaffected.

faq.question: Should I delete server directories to free space?
faq.answer: Do not remove business files directly. Review usage, retention and backups, then use supported cleanup or delete actions.

title: Backups, recovery and audit
summary: Create verified backups and rehearse recovery in isolation.
steps: As owner, create a manual backup and wait for snapshot, compression and verification before downloading.
Configure scheduling and retention as needed, and check successful runs regularly. Backups contain business and account data and require controlled storage and access.
Before recovery, verify the target environment, compatibility and impact. Rehearse in isolation first; a local rehearsal is not a production restore.
Use Audit filters for actor, operation and date to investigate changes. Share times and redacted errors, not credentials or customer data.

faq.question: Is a successful backup download enough?
faq.answer: Also store it safely off-host and verify recovery. Encrypted credentials depend on data-protection keys; confirm key usability when moving between machines.

title: Configuring AI book recognition
summary: Enable assisted recognition and validate its output.
steps: As owner, open Settings → Sign-in and integrations → AI integration. Add or edit a provider, choose its protocol and enter the endpoint, available models and key following that protocol’s field help.
After saving the provider, switch to Business integrations. Assign a provider and image-capable model to book recognition and enable the feature. Saving a provider alone does not enable recognition.
Test with a sample cover and inspect the result. Customers start recognition explicitly and review its output. This assists data entry; it does not automate video production.

faq.question: What should I check if recognition fails?
faq.answer: Check enabled state, endpoint, model, credentials and outbound proxy. Manual entry remains available; model output is not authoritative source material.

title: Notification rules and delivery records
summary: Configure event routing, bilingual templates and alerts.
steps: Open Settings → Messaging → Notifications and choose an event. Check whether it is enabled and who receives it.
Edit and preview both language templates using only supported variables. Check alert level and whether users may mute it before saving.
Owners can inspect delivery records and queues and retry failed events through the provided action. Verify recipients and business state before interpreting a delivery as duplicated.
Set retention for read and archived notifications between 30 and 3650 days as needed. Unread and actionable items are retained; fixed rules such as feedback replies cannot simply be disabled.

faq.question: Does marking a notification read complete the task?
faq.answer: No. Reading and business completion are separate. A revision request requires its actual action, such as resubmission, to be completed.

title: Editing and previewing email templates
summary: Maintain bilingual email content on a dedicated page.
steps: As platform owner, open Settings → Messaging → Email service → Email templates, or search for Email templates in the top bar.
Choose a type and language, then Edit template. Use Preview unsaved changes to check the subject and body without saving or sending mail. Line breaks are preserved.
Choose Save and preview to apply changes. Navigation warns only about actual unsaved edits; type and language remain in the page URL.
Only business notices can be disabled per language. Verification, reset and security messages remain enabled. Disabling blocks unsent notices; skipped notices are not replayed.
Restore defaults saves the default content and enables that language's template. A manually confirmed template test goes to the configured sender with inactive example links.
Filter the audit log by template update, restore or test actions to inspect the actor, time, template type and language.

faq.question: Why are button links not editable?
faq.answer: Links, expiry and security notes are system-generated to protect verification and password recovery.

title: Creating announcements and choosing placement
summary: Configure sign-in notices, personal popups or the customer banner.
steps: Open Project operations → Announcements, create a notice and enter its title and body. Choose Sign-in page, Personal popup or Customer banner. Save a draft, review it, then publish.

Choose the target language and organizations. Signed-in audiences are determined from eligible active accounts at actual publication. Language and organization filters both apply when set. Sign-in notices are not organization-targeted.

Content appears as entered and is not automatically translated. The interface supports Chinese and English and legacy bilingual notices remain readable; review content and audiences for each language.
Set a display duration of 1–3650 days, defaulting to 30, starting at actual publication. Accounts added later do not automatically receive previously published targeted notices.
The customer banner scrolls its title and body and supports pause, details and View all. Dismissal persists for that account across sign-ins and devices; it does not hide future notices.
Published content is locked. To correct it, withdraw the original and create or copy a new notice, which is presented to its target audience again.

faq.question: Why can a customer not see a notice?
faq.answer: Check publication status, placement, expiry, language and organization eligibility at publication, and personal dismissal. The banner shows the newest eligible undismissed notice.

faq.question: Does the organization picker allow member management?
faq.answer: No. The announcement picker only selects recipients and does not grant organization or membership editing permissions.

title: Creating and managing scheduled announcements
summary: Create a notice from Scheduled tasks and track publication.
steps: Open Project operations → Scheduled tasks and choose Create scheduled announcement. Enter the title, body, placement, audience and display duration.
Choose Save and set publication time. The draft is saved first, then the scheduling dialog opens. Select a future time in your device time zone, up to one year ahead.
Confirm to return to Scheduled tasks. Check the pending count, next run and job record. Saving only the draft or closing the scheduling dialog does not create a publication job.
For an existing draft, choose Select draft to schedule and use its Schedule publication action. Scheduled content is locked; cancel the schedule before editing or choosing a new time.
To publish early, find the scheduled notice under Announcements and publish it. Its original schedule will not publish it again. Cancelling retains the draft and cancellation record.
The running service checks due jobs. Missed jobs run after service recovery and maintenance may delay them. Actual publication determines recipients and the display period.

Review succeeded, cancelled and failed jobs under Scheduled tasks. A failed notice returns to draft; inspect content and service health before scheduling again. Refresh uncertain results before repeating publication.

faq.question: Why was the notice not published at the selected time?
faq.answer: Check that the backend service is running, the maintenance state, the selected time zone and job result. Scheduling is not a guarantee of exact-second publication. Records refresh automatically.

faq.question: Can I repeat a notice weekly or run scripts?
faq.answer: Announcement schedules are one-off. Backups have separate recurring settings; this page does not provide arbitrary scripts or general workflow orchestration.

faq.question: Will members added after scheduling receive it?
faq.answer: Recipients are eligible active accounts at actual publication, matching the language and organization filters, rather than a snapshot taken when drafting or scheduling.

title: Checking scheduled backups and run records
summary: Owners can inspect schedules, maintenance pauses and manual runs.
steps: As platform owner, open Project operations → Scheduled tasks. Inspect the backup card for enabled, running or maintenance-paused state and the next run.

Choose Configure to open Backups. Set daily or weekly scheduling, hour, time zone and retention. Backups use their configured time zone, unlike announcement scheduling which uses the device time zone.

For an additional backup, choose Run now and confirm. This creates a manual backup without changing the recurring policy. Another run cannot start while a backup is running or maintenance has paused it.

Switch to Backup records to inspect manual, scheduled and safety backups. For failure, open the error explanation and check storage and service health. Follow the recovery guide to validate successful backups.

faq.question: Why do I only see announcement jobs?
faq.answer: Backups contain business and account data. Their card and records require the platform owner’s runtime permissions.

faq.question: Does a dash for completion time mean failure?
faq.answer: No. Backup records do not currently provide that field. Use the status column to determine the result.
